evidence: The repo lints with flake8, not Ruff: .pre-commit-config.yaml:45 and setup.cfg:87-110 (flake8 with the local Sentry plugin). No unused-argument (ARG) rules are turned on, so CI will not fail on this. In src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:66 IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync is a base default that returns False. Leaving parameters unused there is expected, because the override at issues.py:382 uses both of them.

src/sentry/integrations/example/integration.py:161 does lack **kwargs. But the only caller, src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_status_outbound.py:44-46, passes just (external_issue, is_resolved, project_id) and never passes assignment_source, so no TypeError can happen. The PR passes assignment_source only to sync_assignee_outbound (tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:59-61), and ExampleIntegration.sync_assignee_outbound already accepts **kwargs (example/integration.py:152-158). Side note: adding assignment_source to the abstract sync_status_outbound signature (mixins/issues.py:411-417) looks like it was put in the wrong method, but that is a different issue from the one reported.

src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 has `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. A dataclass default is evaluated once, when the class is defined (at module import), so every AssignmentSource built without an explicit queued, including all from_integration() calls at lines 21-25, gets the same process-start timestamp. Fix: `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. Related: to_dict() (asdict, line 28) passes that datetime into Celery kwargs (utils/sync.py:137-144), which may not serialize under a JSON serializer.

tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:8 is named test_from_dict_empty_array, but line 9 passes an empty dict (`data: dict[str, Any] = {}`). The name is misleading; this is a cosmetic rename only.
tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:13 is named test_from_dict_inalid_data, a typo for 'invalid'. This is a cosmetic rename that doesn't change behavior.
